Excise.Cli.Tests/RedactCommandTests.cs::RunAsync_RedactFlattenOcr_EncryptedSource_PreservesPasswordProtection  # asserts the whole-page Text is EMPTY (structural: flatten-ocr replaces the page with an image, no term claim); the term-specific leak for the same fixture is already SavedPdfLeakScanner-covered by the unencrypted sibling RunAsync_RedactFlattenOcr_ReplacesTheSourceWithCleanImageOnlyOutput and RunRedact_OcrImageText_RemovesASecretBakedOnlyIntoPixels; SavedPdfLeakScanner itself cannot corroborate an ENCRYPTED output (it scans raw/inflated bytes, which are ciphertext regardless of what was redacted)
Excise.Cli.Tests/RedactCommandTests.cs::RunRedact_NoMatch_ReturnsZero_AndOutputExists  # asserts PRESENCE, not absence -- "BANANA" never matched "HELLO WORLD" so nothing was redacted; there is no removal for an independent oracle to corroborate
Excise.Cli.Tests/RedactCommandTests.cs::RunRedact_EncryptedSource_Default_ReEncryptsWithSamePermissions  # output is password-protected; SavedPdfLeakScanner reads raw/inflated bytes, which are ciphertext on an encrypted PDF regardless of whether the term was actually removed, so it cannot corroborate here. Mutool/PdftotextTextExtractor support a --password, but live in Excise.Rendering, which Excise.Cli.Tests does not reference (t0-gates review 2026-09-21; see issue draft for wiring an independent oracle into encrypted-redaction CLI tests)
